title: Capacity-blocked chip-firing from a fixed state: strongly NP-hard on a star
statement: For capacity-blocked chip-firing with an absorbing sink, deciding whether the ordinary normal form of a given admissible initial state is reachable by capacity-legal firings is strongly NP-hard, already on a star: k senders holding bundles a_i (outdegree and capacity a_i) feeding one receiver of outdegree and capacity B. On such a star the reachable states are exactly the bin runs (orders in which every bundle fits into the receiver's current fill, the fill resetting at B), bin runs are exactly decompositions into disjoint blocks of total exactly B followed by an open block of total at most B, and so, when B divides the total, the normal form is reachable iff the bundles partition into groups of total exactly B, which contains 3-PARTITION. On stars the problem is in NP; in general it is in PSPACE. By contrast the all-initial-states version is decided in polynomial time by the weighted dossier's verified decider.
resolves: CBMD-DYN-WEIGHTED-CAPACITY-001 open item: the complexity of transfer from a fixed initial state (the reach-the-normal-form half)
verified: reach_iff, all_fired_reachable_iff, bad_terminal_reachable_iff, run_iff_blocks and normal_form_reachable_iff_partition compile under Lean 4.35.0, Mathlib-free, with no proof escapes and axioms within propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, against the capacity-blocked chip-firing semantics copied verbatim from the weighted dossier.
A semantics custody check confirms every copied declaration is textually identical to the weighted dossier's, and detects a one-symbol mutation.

On 1,208 random stars both compiled decision predicates (exact-bin order exists; some bin run gets stuck) agree with exhaustive simulation, the ordinary normal form is the all-fired state with the total mod B at the receiver, every instance meeting the weighted bound is good, and a run rule that lets bundles cross a multiple of B disagrees with simulation 516 times.

fill_eq_mod, stuck_imp_witness and safe_of_no_witness compile under the same conditions: a stuck bin run leaves the residue (sum of fired bundles) mod B at the receiver, so it yields a residue witness, and the absence of any residue witness certifies that no reachable terminal state is bad.

Exhaustively over every star with B <= 13, k <= 8 (500,461 instances, bundles 1..B, and 1..B+1 for k <= 4), stuck runs exist exactly when residue witnesses do (496,470 instances), the O(kB) residue decider agrees with the witness definition, the bin-run search agrees with exact simulation on 400 random stars, and controls bite: a single-bin rule misses 10,332 stuck instances, a non-strict rule falsely accepts 3,139, largest-fit and smallest-fit greedy runs miss 98,872 and 3,459.

realise_small, realise_pair and bad_of_small_or_pair_witness compile under the same conditions: a residue witness whose unfired senders total at most B, or number exactly two, is realised by a stuck bin run, so a bad terminal state is reachable; in the exhaustive range this covers 492,524 of the 496,470 witness instances, each checked against the model.

An optional C search (bin_runs_exhaustive.c, fired mask as state by fill_eq_mod) finds no counterexample to the residue-witness conjecture over all multisets with B <= 30, k <= 7; B <= 23, k <= 9; B <= 18, k <= 10; B <= 14, k <= 12; and 400,000 random instances with 10 <= B <= 100, 9 <= k <= 16.

spec_iff, dpWitness_iff, dpFast_eq and safe_of_dpFast compile under the same conditions: a table of occurring (residue, smallest unfired bundle) pairs, built one sender at a time in O(kB^2) entries, decides the residue-witness condition exactly, its array-memoised implementation computes the same answer, and a false answer certifies that no reachable terminal state is bad; safe_2_3_3 is such a certificate checked in the kernel. A Python mirror of the table agrees with the witness definition on all 500,461 instances of the exhaustive range.
unresolved: the residue-witness conjecture in the remaining case, where every witness leaves at least three senders unfired with total above B; if true, FIXED-BAD and FIXED-MUST-GOOD on stars are pseudo-polynomial while FIXED-GOOD is strongly NP-hard; FIXED-BAD on general graphs and in binary encoding on stars is open
the exact complexity of FIXED-GOOD in general: NP-hard and in PSPACE, NP membership open because firing vectors can be exponential on digraphs
whether hardness survives with unit multiplicities
nonclaims: the strong NP-hardness of 3-PARTITION is classical and cited, not proved here; what is compiled is the correspondence between the star and exact-bin partitions
NP membership on stars and PSPACE membership in general are written arguments
not a novelty determination; chip-firing reachability hardness (without capacities) and deadlock-avoidance hardness in resource allocation systems are known and are different problems

the residue-witness converse is compiled only for witnesses whose unfired part totals at most B or has two members, otherwise conjectured from exhaustive evidence; the sorted O(kB) decider's equivalence with the witness definition is a written argument checked by enumeration (the O(kB^2) pair-table decider is compiled)
smallest_decisive_test: A star whose normal form is capacity-reachable although its bundles admit no exact-bin partition, or the reverse; or a polynomial algorithm for the star case, which would decide 3-PARTITION.
